study.question: Do fixed-operand original row-sum discrepancies propagate through guarded projection and row scaling into actual accumulated category/brand gradients and represented Adam displacements under total_magnitude, while remaining dormant under none? Baselines have validation AUC0.6050036/0.6102261/0.6133620 (static/pooled/target-aware). Latest magnitude_a/b AUC0.6148846559937464/0.6150147026807334 and loss0.1966748429513674/0.19657392834077755 both lose to none AUC0.6151021885074872, loss0.19653258393542125. All eight prior probes report actual role-sum repeat distances abs8.24e-13..1.99e-12 and rel6.13e-7..1.13e-6, with zero raw/fixed-transform repeats and passing bounded observer checks. Actual Adam mediation, rather than sketch differences, is the consequential missing evidence.
study.hypothesis: At a fixed actual training state, index_add_ floating accumulation variation perturbs q/h, then guarded projected P and sqrt(||P||^2/||G||^2). total_magnitude can transmit it into the detached correction and accumulated table gradient. It may or may not survive Adam conditioning and float32 parameter quantization. None does not use these coefficients and should have zero aggregation-dependent active gradient/update distance. A fixed-tree shadow should be repeatable at identical operands. This is a provisional numerical propagation hypothesis, not a performance gain or established explanation of cross-run AUC drift.

study.proposed_difference: Two standalone schema4 modules share all source except row_intervention. At calls0/1, stable-sort segmented fixed-tree aggregation and a repeated original aggregation are SHADOW alternatives; neither changes active training gradients. Five gradient/real-Adam branches (actual-result, same-coefficient reconstructed no-op, repeated original, fixed-tree, fixed-tree repeat) use one parent BCE graph and cloned exact current table state. If numerical propagation reaches optimization, M original-repeat actual-gradient and represented Adam-step distances are nonzero while raw-repeat, reconstructed no-op and live bridge controls pass. Tiny role changes alone are insufficient.

Fixed-tree repeats have zero role, active-gradient and represented Adam-step distances under passing controls. Original-versus-fixed may differ because floating association changes, without implying the fixed tree has better generalization.
Under none, hypothetical roles/targets may vary but aggregation-dependent active gradients and Adam steps remain exactly equal. Noop/live bridge must pass independently in each execution.

All64 scalars finite; two call snapshots captured at the selected checkpoint, scalar BCE error0 and observer_mutations0. Scope is two early calls through the saved checkpoint; no claim of all-call or cross-execution equality.
falsifiers: Changed mathematical row membership, dtype, valid mask, padding policy or inherited guards defeats attribution. Failed synthetic integer semantics, nonzero mutation/scalar errors or missing optimizer hooks is an implementation/integrity failure, not a model-performance negative.
A nonzero raw-repeat or reconstructed no-op distance prevents clean isolation of the new aggregation contrast. Report these values without assigning all differences to the reducer.
Nonzero live_adam_bridge_bits_mismatches invalidates claims that shadow Adam matches actual table updates, even if a relative distance is small. No tolerance is treated as exact equality.

Stable fixed roles with persisting fixed-repeat gradients/Adam differences reject aggregation as a sufficient source at these sampled states. Equal represented Adam displacements despite different roles/gradients weaken optimizer mediation there.
Any aggregation-specific active gradient/step difference in N conflicts with the intended dormant pathway; investigate implementation/control failure before a mechanism explanation.
Even gated nonzero Adam distances do not establish AUC mediation, a sufficient whole-run numerical cause, a robust magnitude advantage or a superior fixed-tree model.
alternative_explanations: Extra allocations, shadow backward, sorting and optimizer probes can change scheduling despite no mutation. Two-call noop/bridge gates cannot exclude all later observer effects.
Repeated upstream backward or final leaf accumulation, rather than role sums alone, may vary. Raw-repeat, reconstructed noop and live-gradient bridges distinguish part of this alternative.
Small gradient discrepancies may disappear under Adam moments/epsilon and represented parameter quantization; comparison uses double-precision subtraction of represented before/after values.
Near-zero/cancellation-sensitive rows and guard transitions may amplify some differences; aggregate distance and guard mismatch outputs do not reveal a per-row distribution.
Hidden cross-run data/RNG/buffer state, later stochastic execution or checkpoint selection may dominate historical metric variation; within-execution sharing does not certify cross-run state.

Earlier magnitude gains may reflect generic conditioning, adaptive seed42 validation reuse or chance. Historical failures/negative branches remain evidence; repeated same seed executions are not independent mechanism contrasts.
